sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Sell what you have; the point is to learn
sections.para: Start selling now, however rough the product. Expect not to sell: the attempt makes you ship, shows where you are, and starts the feedback loops. A payment is the best signal, paying should be easy from the start, and the first question for a founder is: can you sell it?

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Sell early, learn, make it easy to pay
sections.para: Sell what you have and expect not to; selling makes you ship and gives the best signal. Make paying easy early, do not fear copying, then make customers profitable with atomic purchases and prices you can change.

sections.label: Start selling what you have
sections.line: Go to the end of the journey and sell
sections.para: However rough the product, try to sell it now. As Reid Hoffman said, if the first version does not embarrass you, you launched too late. You might be lucky, but the point is not the sale; it is what you learn.

sections.label: Why selling teaches you
sections.line: Selling makes you ship, and starts the loops
sections.para: Trying to sell forces you to ship, shows where the product really stands, and starts the feedback loops that fix the small problems.

sections.label: The best signal
sections.line: A payment is the best signal, and hard to get
sections.para: Even people with users hesitate to sell. SG/Send paid customers a £5 voucher for £5 of credits and got ten payers in a day, yet they still had to choose to buy. Then they did not come back, the next lesson.

sections.label: Make it easy to pay you
sections.line: Make paying easy from the start
sections.para: Payment is not something added at the end. You can sell at a loss at first; what matters is having customers.

sections.label: Do not worry about being copied
sections.line: Do not fear copying; it is all execution
sections.para: Anyone putting things up for sale is already ahead of most people with ideas. The best lessons came from shipping, selling and iterating.

sections.label: Then make them profitable
sections.line: Then profitable: atomic, changeable, no subscriptions
sections.para: Once there are customers, make them profitable. Keep prices free to change, avoid yearly or monthly contracts, and sell something atomic with a beginning, a middle and an end.

sections.label: Can you sell it?
sections.line: The first question: can you sell it?
sections.para: Every founder Dinis meets gets the same question. The companion piece, start a company, covers where the revenue goes.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: Some products should not be sold before they are safe. Ten customers is not a market, and selling at a loss is a stage, not a model.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A memo, SG/Send's record, and Hoffman
sections.para: Dinis's memo of 19 October 2026, SG/Send's dates from this site, the voucher from the book, and Reid Hoffman's 2017 essay.
